feature: Issue 184: interrupt and redirect a running Codex agent

userStories.title: Measure the locked Codex SDK abort/resume protocol
userStories.description: As an Archon maintainer, I want a bounded credentialed real-SDK spike that records the exact abort terminal shape, event ordering, iterator settlement, thread-id availability, descendant cleanup, and same-thread resume continuity at @openai/codex-sdk 0.144.5 on native Linux, macOS, and Windows, so that Phase 2 implements against measured evidence instead of guessed error matchers.
acceptanceCriteria: `packages/providers/src/codex/interrupt-resume-spike.ts` exists and uses the same SDK entry point as the provider (`startThread().runStreamed()` / `resumeThread(id)`); `packages/providers/package.json` gains a `spike:interrupt:codex` script.

Spike resolves the installed `@openai/codex-sdk` entry + nearest package metadata and requires runtime version exactly `0.144.5` (matching bun.lock); the declared `^0.144.5` range is reported separately.

Probe runs in a disposable `mkdtemp` git repo (unique committed nonce, no access to the project checkout) constrained with `sandboxMode: 'workspace-write'`, `networkAccessEnabled: false`, `approvalPolicy: 'never'`; repo removed in `finally`.

Case A (mid-tool interrupt): retains non-empty thread id from `thread.started`, captures all descendant PIDs of the spike process immediately before abort, aborts the dedicated SDK controller while the command is still active, records event types + relative order and the exact terminal discriminant (constructor/name + stable sanitized message fragments), and requires the async iterator to settle within an explicit timeout.
Case B (early operator intent): marks intent before `thread.started`, defers the real controller abort until the id is retained, and produces the same terminal class plus a non-empty id.

Case C (resume continuity): three bounded interrupt/resume cycles total; every resume calls `resumeThread()` with the interrupted id (never `startThread()`), and each completes naturally demonstrating prior context (nonce + follow-up value).

Case D (cleanup): platform process-table traversal captures every descendant (PID+PPID+start fingerprint on POSIX, PowerShell/CIM equivalent on native Windows); after settlement + bounded cleanup interval all captured descendants are gone; survivors are SIGTERMed then SIGKILLed only after re-verifying the start fingerprint; zero unhandledRejection/uncaughtException recorded (temporary recorders installed before first SDK call, restored in finally — any event is a hard failure).

Sanitized report committed at `plans/260920-0216-issue-184-interrupt-and-redirect-codex-agent/reports/codex-interrupt-resume-spike.md`: one section per OS family (date, OS/arch, Bun version, declared range, locked version, resolved runtime), event-order summaries for A and B, exact sanitized terminal variant per OS (narrow discriminants per variant, not a merged broad matcher), settlement times, thread-id-before-abort result, descendant cleanup counts/elapsed, all three resume results, rejection/exception counts, final PASS or BLOCKED with a reason per failed field. No prompt text, tokens, thread ids, home paths, or command content.
Missing credentials, missing binary, wrong SDK version, or an untested OS family is recorded as BLOCKED, not skipped or passed. WSL evidence is filed under Linux, never Windows.
No production behavior changed: `CODEX_CAPABILITIES`, `CodexProvider`, and `dag-executor.ts` are untouched; `cd packages/providers && bun x tsc --noEmit` passes.
userStories.technicalNotes: Implements plan Phase 1 verbatim (`phase-01-codex-stream-abort-seam-and-real-sdk-gate.md`). This is a diagnostic gate, not a feature prototype — do not flip capabilities or touch provider/executor code. Bound every iterator settlement and resumed turn with explicit timeouts; never leave a promise or child running after a failed assertion. If any gate item fails on any required OS family, record BLOCKED and stop; Phase 2 (US-002) may not start. Verification: `cd packages/providers && bun run spike:interrupt:codex && bun x tsc --noEmit`. Inspect the report for secrets/ids/absolute paths before committing it.

userStories.title: Codex provider/executor interrupt slice with strict same-thread resume
userStories.description: As a workflow operator, I want Stop to end only the active Codex turn (never node Cancel), preserve the thread id for resumability, and have the next guidance turn resume that exact thread, so that interrupt/redirect works for Codex exactly as it does for Claude without silently starting a fresh conversation.
acceptanceCriteria: Gate: `reports/codex-interrupt-resume-spike.md` shows PASS on every required item for native Linux, macOS, and Windows; every 'measured abort terminal' reference in this work is replaced by the exact observed variant(s) (narrow enumerated per-OS discriminants if they differ). A BLOCKED report means this story does not proceed.

`packages/providers/src/types.ts` exports `STREAM_ABORT_TERMINAL_REASON = 'stream_aborted'`; docs updated so `MessageChunk.terminalReason` may be provider-native or provider-normalized, `interruptSignal` covers native and stream-abort providers, and explicit `forkSession:false` means in-place continuation. No new request field added.

`CodexProvider.sendQuery()` keeps per-attempt local state (`knownThreadId` seeded `thread.id ?? resumeSessionId`, `operatorInterruptRequested`, `operatorAbortForwarded`, existing fresh `attemptController`); node `abortSignal` aborts the attempt immediately and wins at every catch/terminal boundary (`Query aborted`); operator `interruptSignal` forwards the abort only once a non-empty `knownThreadId` exists — on a fresh thread intent is held until the normalizer consumes `thread.started`; both listeners removed in `finally` (never abort the attempt controller merely as cleanup, per #1735).

Terminal classification emits `{type:'result', sessionId: knownThreadId, terminalReason: STREAM_ABORT_TERMINAL_REASON}` only when node Cancel is not set AND `operatorAbortForwarded` is true for this attempt AND the terminal matches the Phase-1-measured variant; a natural `turn.completed` racing Stop stays natural with normal usage; an unrelated `turn.failed`/unknown throw stays a real failure; `SUBPROCESS_CRASH_PATTERNS` is never used for this classification; no usage/stopReason/error subtype invented on the marker.

After the SDK controller is aborted the stream keeps consuming buffered events so an already-buffered `item.completed` still yields a successful `tool_result`; no operator-interrupt checks between arbitrary events.

Retry/backoff: node Cancel then operator-interrupt outcome are checked before `classifyAndEnrichCodexError()`; once operator intent exists no error from that turn cold-retries; the retry sleep is replaced by an abort-aware delay whose timer/listeners are cleaned up, and Stop during backoff ends the sequence immediately throwing the retained unmarked error (never the marker); calls with neither signal keep existing retry behavior.

Strict in-place resume: when `resumeSessionId !== undefined && requestOptions?.forkSession === false`, a synchronous `resumeThread()` failure is enriched and thrown (no `startThread()`, no 'Starting fresh conversation'); the skill-catalog compatibility path may recreate the client but must `resumeThread()` the same id or fail; a retryable subprocess crash fails instead of reaching the attempt>0 `startThread()` branch. `forkSession` omitted/true keeps existing best-effort fallback + warning unchanged.

`packages/workflows/src/dag-executor.ts` imports the shared constant and adds it to `INTERRUPT_TERMINAL_REASONS` with no provider-name conditional; `packages/providers/src/codex/capabilities.ts` flips `interrupt` to `'stream-abort'` in the same green revision — no reviewable state advertises the capability without executor recognition or vice versa.

Provider tests (`provider.test.ts`, existing mockStartThread/mockResumeThread/mockRunStreamed fixtures) cover all 12 plan cases: capability declaration + snapshot; post-`thread.started` stop → one marker with new id, no retry; pending stop on new thread waits for id; resumed-thread/pre-aborted stop → marker without `runStreamed()`; buffered `item.completed` after abort still yields `tool_result` before marker; natural race stays natural; measured shape without forwarded-abort and unknown error after Stop are real failures; Cancel wins co-fire → `Query aborted`; Stop during backoff surfaces retained error with no further spawn; listeners/timers detached after success/interrupt/failure; strict resume refuses all three cold-start doors with explicit error and zero `startThread()` calls; omitted `forkSession` keeps fallback. All pre-existing tests stay green.

Executor conformance (`dag-executor.test.ts`, reusing Story 2.3 helpers, test provider returns `getType() === 'codex'` so the real registry exposes the handle): direct Codex node — open tool settles `interrupted` once, one interrupted row, node stays `running`, `generating → idle-after-interrupt`, then Send-now drains queued+new receipts in order with `resumeSessionId === 'sess-1'` and `forkSession === false`; unmarked Codex crash with operator flag set still fails; AI loop resumes `sess-1` in the same iteration without consuming an extra iteration; loop-group body parks/resumes under its namespaced step key.

Verification passes: `cd packages/providers && bun test src/codex/provider.test.ts && bun test src/registry.test.ts`; `cd ../workflows && bun test src/dag-executor.test.ts -t 'Codex interrupt' && bun test src/dag-executor.test.ts && bun test src/steering-registry.test.ts`; `bun run type-check` and `bun run lint --max-warnings 0` from repo root.
No server route, steering-registry, web, schema, or database file is modified; `mockCodexCapabilities` in dag-executor.test.ts is not edited as the feature gate.
userStories.technicalNotes: Implements plan Phase 2 verbatim (`phase-02-executor-marker-and-codex-conformance.md`). TDD order: red provider tests → export marker + implement provider (capability stays false while behavior goes green) → red executor conformance tests → teach executor the marker → flip `interrupt:'stream-abort'` so the first green state is fully enabled. If the mocked implementation needs a broader classifier than the spike supports, rerun/extend the spike instead of guessing. If deferred abort can't retain the id without losing events/hanging, keep capability false and report the blocker. Rollback path: capability back to `false` + remove provider interrupt wiring; executor marker stays inert.

userStories.title: Truthful stop disclosure across canonical UX and both shipped shells
userStories.description: As an operator, I want the idle-after-interrupt disclosure to state that in-flight work may be partial, so that the UI never claims Stop only acts at a completed-tool boundary — which Codex stream-abort disproves.
acceptanceCriteria: The literal `stopped after the last completed tool call · files already written stay written` is replaced by `turn stopped · in-flight work may be partial · written files stay written` in every current/authoritative artifact: `_bmad-output/specs/spec-agent-node-room/SPEC.md` ('Interrupt is not undo' amended so it does not promise session state only through a completed tool), `control-states.md`, `EXPERIENCE.md` (all three normative copy/state/journey occurrences, voice/placement preserved), `DESIGN.md` (one-line typography/anatomy unchanged), `mockups/key-steering-dock.html`, `claude-design/design_handoff_node_room_transcript_steering/README.md`, and the three `*.dc.html` handoff prototypes (Console Node Room, Legacy Node Room, Steering Dock States).

Historical inputs are untouched: `sources/spec-live-agent-steering/`, dated accessibility/rubric reports, `.working/` mockups. Any other generated/current artifact containing the old literal is classified before editing — no indiscriminate repo-wide replace.
`packages/web/src/lib/steering-dock.ts` changes only `STEERING_INTERRUPT_DISCLOSURE`; no component structure or CSS changes anywhere.

Test assertions updated to the new exact literal: `steering-dock.test.ts` pins the shared value; `ComposerDock.test.tsx` (Legacy idle), `NodeTranscriptPane.test.tsx` (Legacy room), `ConsoleComposerDock.test.tsx` (Console idle), `ConsoleNodeRoom.test.tsx` (Console room).

`e2e/ui/agent-interrupt-redirect.spec.ts` expects the new literal and retains/extends two-shell evidence: Generating keeps Stop/Queue positions with QUEUED band and no disclosure; Interrupting keeps `Stopping…` focusable with `aria-disabled` (never native `disabled`), focus does not fall to `<body>`, reduced motion honored; Idle shows Stop absent, `Send now`, `WILL SEND` band, disclosure once between band and field (or above field with no band), open tool row `⚠ interrupted` not failed; Generating-again removes the disclosure and restores controls without horizontal movement or row/order change.

Viewport evidence: Legacy at 460px authored room width and Console at its 520px authored reference panel width each keep the disclosure a single legible line wholly inside the dock with no horizontal overflow; both shells at 460×900 responsive stay inside the viewport with no overlap/clip/wrap; existing 1440×900 full-room captures preserved for context (room's measured width used as evidence, not raw viewport width).

Playwright run uses the existing fake provider (UI consumes provider-independent sub-state; no live credentials in browser tests) and is executed with `ARCHON_E2E_PROOF=1 npx playwright test -c playwright.config.ts ui/agent-interrupt-redirect.spec.ts` from `e2e/`; if the e2e package isn't installed, its documented `npm ci`/browser setup is used — an unsupported or skipped run is not counted as passing evidence.
If the new copy cannot hold the one-line geometry, the copy is adjusted in the canonical UX artifacts first — never silently shrink type, clip text, or diverge the two shells.
Focused gates pass: `cd packages/web && bun test src/lib/steering-dock.test.ts` and `NODE_ENV=development bun test` for all four component test files listed above.
userStories.technicalNotes: Implements the copy/UI half of plan Phase 3 (`phase-03-closeout-matrix-docs-sprint-status.md`, sections 'Copy decision', 'Canonical product and UX authority', 'Shipped UI and tests', 'Visual and interaction acceptance'). Order: canonical SPEC/control-state and UX design/experience copy first, then current mockup/handoff artifacts, then shared web constant + unit/integration assertions, then the Playwright spec + proof run. Do NOT update steering-test-plan.md, provider-steering-matrix.md, generated capability docs, acceptance.md, or sprint-status.yaml here — that is US-004.

userStories.title: Provider evidence docs, generated capability matrix, acceptance record, sprint closeout
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want measured evidence published into the spec companions and generated docs, an acceptance report mapping every AC to its proof, and sprint status flipped only after all gates pass, so that Story 2.4 closes with an auditable record.
acceptanceCriteria: `_bmad-output/specs/spec-agent-node-room/steering-test-plan.md` replaces the provisional Codex 'pins shape' bullet with the measured terminal shape, the normalized `stream_aborted` marker, strict same-thread behavior, and references to the named tests + spike report; its UI-section disclosure expectation matches the new literal. No reliability claim beyond the measured three cycles.

`_bmad-output/specs/spec-agent-node-room/provider-steering-matrix.md` changes Codex evidence to measured, cites the plan-local spike report, describes deferred-id abort / no-cold-retry / strict resume, and removes the inaccurate `startThread` fallback statement for the guidance path.

`bun run generate:capability-matrix` is run and `packages/docs-web/src/content/docs/reference/provider-capabilities.md` is regenerated (never hand-edited) showing Codex 'Turn interrupt' = `stream-abort`; `bun run check:capability-matrix` passes.

`plans/260920-0216-issue-184-interrupt-and-redirect-codex-agent/reports/acceptance.md` maps each plan/Story 2.4 acceptance criterion to named tests, spike report fields, visual evidence, and commands with their actual results; it records the residual operational risk that Stop is not undo, and does NOT record same-thread fallback or inaccurate disclosure as accepted gaps (this plan fixed them).

Integrated re-verification passes: `cd packages/providers && bun test src/codex/provider.test.ts`; `cd ../workflows && bun test src/dag-executor.test.ts -t 'Codex interrupt'`; the four focused web test invocations; the Playwright scenario; `bun run generate:capability-matrix`, `bun run check:capability-matrix`, and root `bun run validate` (which does not cover the standalone e2e package — both gates required).

`_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/agent-node-room/sprint-status.yaml` moves Story 2.4 from `backlog` to `done` ONLY as the final edit after every gate above is green; formatting/generated checks are re-run after that edit.
userStories.technicalNotes: Implements the closeout half of plan Phase 3 (`phase-03-closeout-matrix-docs-sprint-status.md`, 'Provider evidence and closeout' file table and Steps 4-8). Capability-matrix output is machine-owned: regenerating only the markdown while keeping the capability flip fails `check:capability-matrix`. Sprint status flips last, after all evidence exists.
